Cull-first individual-dive model

Nested site effects and expanded-window sensitivity

Interpretation

Both linkage directions are retained because they answer different questions:

  • Cull-first: every eligible cull dive uses its most recent preceding eDNA event. This retains 2,117 dives but allows one eDNA event to inform multiple later culls.
  • eDNA-first: each sampling campaign uses only the first subsequent visit to every cull site. This gives 519 non-duplicated visits but intentionally excludes later visits.

The cull-first hierarchy is:

COTS count ~ % positive + distance + elapsed time
             + offset(log(bottom time))
             + (1 | reef) + (1 | cull site) + (1 | eDNA event)

reef_site 2117 -6667.282 13348.56 1.176 0.635 NA 1.874 0 TRUE 276.516

Adding cull site improves AIC by 288 relative to reef only. Adding the eDNA event effect improves AIC by another 277 relative to site-only and prevents repeated exposure to one molecular event being treated as independent information.

Cull-first BRMS model

The production fit has 8,000 post-warmup draws, all R-hat values are 1.00, and no divergent transitions. Percent positive is clearly positive, elapsed time is clearly negative, and the remaining additive distance effect is close to zero.

term Estimate Est.Error Q2.5 Q97.5
Intercept -4.073 0.213 -4.511 -3.671
edna_prop_z 0.441 0.078 0.289 0.599
distance_z -0.006 0.040 -0.083 0.073
lag_z -0.207 0.027 -0.260 -0.153

The marginal 0.04 crossing is approximately 75% positive for cull-first and 73% for eDNA-first.

Expanded 5 km / 365-day window

window n_cull_dives n_reefs n_cull_sites n_edna_events median_distance_m median_lag_days
2,000 m / 183 days 2117 36 332 165 478.6 77
5,000 m / 365 days 3650 45 518 214 739.9 125

The expanded window adds 1,533 dives, nine reefs and 186 sites. Flexible distance and time functions are strongly preferred to the original log-linear additive formulation.

model n logLik AIC convergence_code positive_definite_hessian delta_AIC
spline_degradation 3650 -11186.50 22409.00 0 TRUE 0.00
spline_additive 3650 -11196.72 22417.44 0 TRUE 8.45
additive_log 3650 -11214.87 22445.74 0 TRUE 36.74
linear_degradation 3650 -11213.48 22446.95 0 TRUE 37.96

The spline degradation model allows the percent-positive association itself to change over distance and time. It is favoured by 8.4 AIC units over additive splines. The fitted contrast is strongest around 1-2 km and weaker by 5 km, rather than declining monotonically from zero distance. At 5 km and 365 days, the expected curve is nearly flat and its uncertainty is wide. This may reflect signal degradation, but could also reflect cull-site selection relative to eDNA locations.

Recommendation

Retain 2 km / 183 days as the primary operational window for now. The expanded window is useful for studying persistence boundaries, but its flexible shape should be tested with complete eDNA events held out before operational use. Present cull-first and eDNA-first results together as linkage sensitivity analyses rather than selecting one solely because it has more rows.
